questions.stem: Which Terraform address matches the web entry in CLZ-250's vm_definitions map?

options.A: azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.web[0]
options.B: azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.web["web"]
options.C: azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.web["Standard_B2s"]
options.D: azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.web.role

optionExplanations.A: That is a count-style numeric address.
optionExplanations.B: Map keys supply the instance identities used by for_each.
optionExplanations.C: VM size is a value, not the chosen key.
optionExplanations.D: The Role tag is metadata, not an individual resource address.

questions.stem: A new batch map entry must provide which attributes to fit CLZ-250's typed vm_definitions input?

options.A: minimum, default, and maximum as numbers
options.B: frontend_port and backend_port only
options.C: Only a Windows password as a string
options.D: vm_size and role as strings

optionExplanations.A: Those are autoscale capacity attributes from a later lesson.
optionExplanations.B: Those describe port forwarding, not the VM definition object.
optionExplanations.C: The administrator password is generated separately.
optionExplanations.D: Each map value is an object containing those two attributes.

questions.stem: Why does a NIC reference azurerm_public_ip.web[each.key].id?

options.A: To attach the public IP belonging to the same named map entry
options.B: To attach the alphabetically first public IP to every NIC
options.C: To allocate a public IP inside each VM's password
options.D: To change the map key to the public IP's numeric address

optionExplanations.A: The key aligns corresponding network resource instances.
optionExplanations.B: The expression selects the current key.
optionExplanations.C: Credentials are unrelated to IP association.
optionExplanations.D: The expression does not redefine for_each identity.

questions.stem: The web object specifies Standard_B2s and batch specifies another valid SKU. Which expression lets the VMs differ in size?

options.A: size = each.value.vm_size
options.B: size = each.key
options.C: size = count.index
options.D: size = length(var.vm_definitions)

optionExplanations.A: Each instance reads its own object value.
optionExplanations.B: The key is a workload name, not a SKU.
optionExplanations.C: This block uses for_each and does not have count.index.
optionExplanations.D: The number of entries is not a VM size.

questions.stem: A learner changes only the web entry's role from web to frontend. What remains the Terraform identity?

options.A: The new Role tag frontend
options.B: The generated administrator password
options.C: The position where web appears in the map text
options.D: The map key web

optionExplanations.A: Tags are metadata; they are not for_each keys.
optionExplanations.B: Passwords do not identify the Terraform instance.
optionExplanations.C: Map identity is not based on textual ordering.
optionExplanations.D: Changing a value attribute does not rename the key.

questions.stem: The ops entry is removed while web remains unchanged. What should the plan normally do?

options.A: Delete web because it is the first alphabetical entry
options.B: Delete the keyed ops resources and preserve the unchanged web identities
options.C: Rename web to ops automatically
options.D: Only remove the Role tag while retaining every ops resource

optionExplanations.A: for_each does not remove objects by index position.
optionExplanations.B: Each key controls its corresponding VM, NIC, IP, and association.
optionExplanations.C: Removing a key does not rename another key.
optionExplanations.D: The removed key no longer describes those resource instances.

questions.stem: A valid batch entry is added to vm_definitions. What should a learner expect in the plan?

options.A: Renumbering web and ops into [1] and [2]
options.B: Only one additional Terraform output string and no Azure resources
options.C: New resources addressed with the batch key
options.D: A replacement of all existing VMs solely due to map insertion

optionExplanations.A: Named identities do not become numeric indexes.
optionExplanations.B: The map drives VM and networking resource creation.
optionExplanations.C: The repetition uses one resource instance per map key.
optionExplanations.D: Unchanged keys need not be replaced by an added entry.

questions.stem: A learner renames the map key web to frontend without a moved block. Why does the plan propose delete/create?

options.A: Role tags cannot contain the word frontend
options.B: The old and new keys are different Terraform instance addresses
options.C: Azure forbids changing any configuration file
options.D: for_each only accepts one key

optionExplanations.A: The issue is identity, not that role value.
optionExplanations.B: Terraform cannot infer that a renamed key should preserve the existing object.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform supports changes, subject to resource semantics.
optionExplanations.D: The lesson allows a small map of multiple entries.

questions.stem: During a real key refactor, what can a moved block communicate to Terraform?

options.A: That a former instance address corresponds to a new instance address
options.B: That all future VM size changes must be ignored
options.C: That the guest RDP port should become 443
options.D: That the Terraform password should be removed from every backup

optionExplanations.A: It preserves state identity through a documented address move when applicable.
optionExplanations.B: That is not the purpose of moved blocks.
optionExplanations.C: Address moves do not configure guest services.
optionExplanations.D: A moved block does not sanitize stored secrets.

questions.stem: A rename affects a VM, its NIC, public IP, and NSG association. What should the refactor review cover?

options.A: Only the VM's Role tag
options.B: Only the browser quiz score
options.C: Address mappings and planned changes for every affected resource
options.D: Only the README heading, without a Terraform plan

optionExplanations.A: Other keyed resource addresses are affected as well.
optionExplanations.B: Progress data has no effect on Terraform identity.
optionExplanations.C: The related resource graph also uses the renamed key.
optionExplanations.D: The infrastructure changes must be inspected.

questions.stem: Can for_each use map keys that are unknown until a new Azure resource is created?

options.A: Yes; it creates every possible key in the subscription
options.B: Yes; only the map's Role tags must be known
options.C: No; because for_each never accepts maps
options.D: No; Terraform must know instance keys before remote operations

optionExplanations.A: Terraform does not enumerate arbitrary future keys.
optionExplanations.B: The identities themselves must be known.
optionExplanations.C: Maps are a primary supported input.
optionExplanations.D: The planner needs stable known identities to construct instances.

questions.stem: Why should credentials not be used as for_each keys?

options.A: Keys are exposed as resource identities and sensitive values cannot be used for for_each identity
options.B: Keys are encrypted into the VM's managed disk automatically
options.C: Every key becomes an administrator password by default
options.D: The Role tag is the only visible identity anywhere

optionExplanations.A: Instance addressing must not reveal secrets.
optionExplanations.B: Resource addresses are not encrypted guest storage.
optionExplanations.C: Keys do not supply authentication unless configured as a value.
optionExplanations.D: Plans and state expose instance keys as addresses.

questions.stem: Why does CLZ-250 use a map of objects rather than just a set of workload names?

options.A: A set of strings cannot be used with for_each in any Terraform configuration
options.B: Each named workload needs its own size and role values
options.C: Maps hide all resource identities from plans
options.D: Objects prevent Azure from charging for compute

optionExplanations.A: Terraform supports string sets, but this lesson needs richer values.
optionExplanations.B: Typed object values carry configuration beyond identity.
optionExplanations.C: Map keys appear in addresses.
optionExplanations.D: Data types do not change Azure billing.

questions.stem: A learner adds batch = { vm_size = "Standard_B2s" } but omits role. Why does the typed input fail?

options.A: Terraform requires every object to include a public IP literal
options.B: Windows size strings must be numeric
options.C: The object does not satisfy the required role attribute
options.D: The batch key must be the first item in the map

optionExplanations.A: The public IP is created by another resource.
optionExplanations.B: The input expects a SKU string.
optionExplanations.C: Every entry needs both string attributes.
optionExplanations.D: Map order is not this constraint.

questions.stem: The learner rearranges the same web and ops map entries without changing keys or values. What should identity do?

options.A: Remain based on the same named keys
options.B: Switch from web to ops at index zero
options.C: Rotate every generated password due to sorting
options.D: Create duplicate VMs for both orderings

optionExplanations.A: Reordering textual map entries does not change their identity.
optionExplanations.B: This is not a count-based list.
optionExplanations.C: Text order alone does not request credential replacement.
optionExplanations.D: The map still contains the same two keys.

questions.stem: Why is windows_vm_public_ips a map keyed by workload name in CLZ-250?

options.A: Because every output must be a map in Terraform
options.B: Because public IP resources cannot use numeric addresses
options.C: Because it contains administrator passwords instead of IP addresses
options.D: It preserves the correspondence between each identity and its public endpoint

optionExplanations.A: Outputs can have many value types.
optionExplanations.B: Public IPs have numeric IP values; the map keys provide labels.
optionExplanations.C: The output is an endpoint map, not a credential store.
optionExplanations.D: Named outputs help validate the same keys used by the resources.

questions.stem: Which Azure observation shows that each.value.role is actually used by the implementation?

options.A: The VM's public IP ends in the role name
options.B: Each VM's Role tag matches its map entry
options.C: The Windows RDP login screen automatically names the role
options.D: The Terraform binary changes its filename to the role

optionExplanations.A: IP numbers do not encode the Role tag.
optionExplanations.B: The code merges Role into resource tags from the object value.
optionExplanations.C: Guest login display is not evidence of Azure tagging.
optionExplanations.D: Binary filenames are independent of map values.

questions.stem: Which lesson command helps confirm that named keys replaced positional count addresses?

options.A: terraform state list with a filter for quoted keys
options.B: terraform fmt with the -recursive flag
options.C: az account list alone
options.D: Test-NetConnection against the resource-group name

optionExplanations.A: The resulting addresses should contain keys such as ["web"].
optionExplanations.B: Formatting does not show tracked resource identities.
optionExplanations.C: That lists account context rather than Terraform addresses.
optionExplanations.D: A connectivity test is not an identity listing.

questions.stem: The named VMs have public IPs for this teaching pattern. Which administration input still must be supplied?

options.A: An Internet-wide /0 to ensure every keyed VM works
options.B: A distinct Azure subscription GUID for each map key
options.C: The current administrator's real public IPv4 /32
options.D: The Role tag as a firewall source

optionExplanations.A: The lesson rejects a broad RDP source.
optionExplanations.B: All instances can exist in the selected lesson subscription.
optionExplanations.C: Public reachability must retain the lesson's narrow RDP source rule.
optionExplanations.D: Metadata is not a network CIDR.

questions.stem: Why can two map entries have different ongoing compute costs?

options.A: Alphabetically later keys always receive a discount
options.B: Each value can select a different vm_size
options.C: Only the Role tag decides the compute bill
options.D: for_each makes all VMs free after the first entry

optionExplanations.A: Key sorting does not set Azure price.
optionExplanations.B: Different sizes can have different price and capacity requirements.
optionExplanations.C: Tags support organization, not SKU pricing.
optionExplanations.D: Each running VM is separately billable.

questions.stem: A learner supplies an empty vm_definitions map. Why does CLZ-250 reject it?

options.A: Terraform for_each globally forbids empty maps
options.B: Azure requires the names web and ops in every VM deployment
options.C: An empty map automatically creates a sixth VM
options.D: The lesson requires one through five validated entries

optionExplanations.A: Generic for_each can accept an empty map.
optionExplanations.B: Those defaults are not Azure requirements.
optionExplanations.C: An empty collection does not imply extra instances.
optionExplanations.D: The bounds keep a meaningful and limited learning set.

questions.stem: The pattern will be reused in several environments. What production improvement reduces repeated implementation code?

options.A: Copying tfstate into every folder as a template
options.B: A module with a clear typed input contract
options.C: Renaming all keys to the same word
options.D: Removing input validation so each environment can guess the shape

optionExplanations.A: Copying state can duplicate ownership and expose secrets.
optionExplanations.B: A module can encapsulate the VM and networking pattern while retaining named inputs.
optionExplanations.C: A map needs distinct keys; identical identities cannot describe separate entries.
optionExplanations.D: Explicit contracts reduce ambiguity.

questions.stem: Only the batch entry's chosen SKU lacks regional quota. What corrective approach fits this lesson?

options.A: Rename every key to force quota to refresh
options.B: Change every Role tag to quota-approved
options.C: Remove the state file so Azure ignores limits
options.D: Choose an approved available size for batch and review the new plan

optionExplanations.A: Resource names do not create quota.
optionExplanations.B: Tags cannot reserve capacity.
optionExplanations.C: State deletion cannot bypass Azure quota.
optionExplanations.D: The per-entry value lets the adjustment stay focused.

questions.stem: The VMs use different Role tags. Does that alone give each role a different NSG rule set?

options.A: Yes; Azure interprets the Role tag as an NSG template
options.B: Yes; each.value.role replaces every NSG destination port
options.C: No; the implementation attaches the same web NSG to each NIC
options.D: No; because tagged NICs cannot have NSGs

optionExplanations.A: There is no such automatic tag-to-policy mapping here.
optionExplanations.B: The code does not use role to define ports.
optionExplanations.C: Tags do not automatically create role-specific filtering.
optionExplanations.D: NICs can have tags and NSG associations.

questions.stem: Which design change belongs in a production version of CLZ-250?

options.A: Private administration and an explicit approved egress path instead of direct VM public access
options.B: Universal RDP access so every role can be tested
options.C: Publishing the keyed IP map together with administrator credentials
options.D: Removing the VNet because for_each keys isolate workloads

optionExplanations.A: The README labels public NIC IPs as an educational exception.
optionExplanations.B: Broad administration access is not the production guidance.
optionExplanations.C: Credentials must not be made public.
optionExplanations.D: Terraform identity is not network isolation.

questions.learningObjective: Use values rather than identity for routine metadata edits
questions.stem: A learner only wants a different descriptive role for ops. Which input change preserves its key?

options.A: Rename ops to the new role on every resource automatically
options.B: Replace for_each with count without planning a state refactor
options.C: Delete every map entry except web
options.D: Edit vm_definitions.ops.role while keeping the ops key

optionExplanations.A: Changing a key changes its Terraform address.
optionExplanations.B: That changes the identity model.
optionExplanations.C: That removes resources rather than editing metadata.
optionExplanations.D: Routine metadata changes need not rename the instance.

questions.stem: What should be reviewed before applying a plan that removes ops?

options.A: Only whether the word ops appears in the book
options.B: Only the order of the map's closing braces
options.C: All resources addressed by ops and any dependent changes
options.D: Only the local PowerShell window color

optionExplanations.A: Book text does not describe the Terraform actions.
optionExplanations.B: Syntax layout is not the resource change.
optionExplanations.C: Removal affects the VM and related keyed network resources.
optionExplanations.D: UI colors do not show deletion scope.

questions.stem: Does using readable map keys remove the need to protect the generated Windows password in state?

options.A: No; stable identities and secret protection solve different problems
options.B: Yes; only count resources can contain sensitive values
options.C: Yes; map keys encrypt every object attribute
options.D: No; because Role tags themselves always contain passwords

optionExplanations.A: State can retain guest credentials regardless of repetition model.
optionExplanations.B: for_each resources can also store secrets in state.
optionExplanations.C: Keys do not provide encryption.
optionExplanations.D: Role is ordinary metadata here.

questions.stem: After destroy removes the outputs, how can the learner verify the intended group is absent?

options.A: Use an arbitrary group name from a previous lesson
options.B: Use the resource-group name captured before destroy in az group exists
options.C: Only check that the output map was printed once
options.D: Resolve the Role tag in public DNS

optionExplanations.A: That can verify the wrong target.
optionExplanations.B: The saved identity supports a precise independent check.
optionExplanations.C: Printing an output does not prove deletion.
optionExplanations.D: Tags are not public DNS records.

questions.learningObjective: Compare named VMs with a fleet model
questions.stem: When should the team consider VMSS instead of many distinct for_each VMs?

options.A: When every server must retain a unique long-lived individual role and configuration
options.B: When a Role tag must be added to only one VM
options.C: When the instances should be interchangeable members of one scalable workload
options.D: When map textual ordering changes

optionExplanations.A: That is a reason to consider distinct keyed identities.
optionExplanations.B: A tag edit alone does not require VMSS.
optionExplanations.C: VMSS applies a common fleet model rather than maintaining distinct named servers.
optionExplanations.D: Named-map order does not require a new compute abstraction.
